files.credit: NASA Earth Observatory - Blue Marble Next Generation (Reto Stöckli)
files.processing: resized from 5400x2700 to 4096x2048 (System.Drawing HighQualityBicubic, JPEG quality 90). July 2004 monthly composite with topography + bathymetry (world.topo.bathy.200407; Visible Earth record 73751 now redirects to the NASA Science page). Longitude -180° at the left edge: verified from the matching GeoTIFF (tie point -180, +90; 0.0667°/px; EPSG:4326) and visually (Greenwich in the centre). Not shifted.

files.credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (CGI Moon Kit, Ernie Wright); LRO LROC WAC colour mosaic: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University (LROC team); polar fill from LRO LOLA
files.processing: converted from TIFF (24-bit RGB, LZW, 4096x2048) to JPEG quality 90 without resampling. This is the 2019 colour map; SVS added a brighter 2025 16-bit version (lroc_color_16bit_srgb_4k.tif), which was also tested but looks washed-out without lighting. SVS: 'The map is centered on 0° longitude' -> -180° at the left edge; verified visually (Mare Crisium at about +59°, Tycho at about -11°). Not shifted.

files.processing: read lines 11570-12469 and samples 527-2176 (1-based) of the 52224x5064 16-bit calibrated frame (camera geometry, not map-projected) with an HTTP range request; linear stretch of scaled I/F DN 92-2187 (0.3rd-99.9th percentile) to 8-bit; resized 1650x900 to 1200x900 (across-track 0.40 m to 0.55 m per pixel so pixels are square, HighQualityBicubic); turned 180° so north is up and east is right (LROC data node corners: first line at 8.12° N, sample 1 at 33.24° E; the shadow falls under the east wall as the east-southeast Sun predicts); JPEG quality 90 (System.Drawing).
